notes: Reconstructed directly from positives/ on Della (word_count = whitespace-split token count of the raw .txt file). Supersedes the sandbox-estimated word counts in HANDOFF_della.md's per-author table, which were approximate. 2026-09-29 expansion: added Richardson Pilgrimage vols 4-9 (1919-1927) and Ford's Parade's End vols 1-2 (1924-25) so the non-Woolf authors have career arcs long enough for the work-to-work comparison the chapter makes about Woolf. Richardson now spans 1915-1927 (9 works) against Woolf's 1915-1941 (10 works). Ford's tetralogy stays incomplete: vols 3-4 are not on Gutenberg. Faulkner cannot be extended from Gutenberg at all (only The Sound and the Fury is there), so he remains a 2-work, 1929-30 snapshot. Added May Sinclair (8 works, 1897-1922) — she used 'stream of consciousness' as a critical term in 1918 reviewing Richardson, and the arc is chosen to straddle that coinage. Every entry now also carries the fields verify_corpus.py checks: gutenberg_id, volume (where asserted), sha256/opening (pinned contents), title_on_titlepage, and provenance_note for the non-Gutenberg files. Publication years are asserted from scholarship, not from Gutenberg — dcterms:issued is the PG posting date, so years can only be bounded by the author's lifespan, not confirmed. Second pass 2026-09-29: added Henry James at four career points (1875-1904, 5 files since Portrait of a Lady is two Gutenberg volumes). The first pass left every male author a 1-8 year snapshot while Woolf, Richardson and Sinclair all gained arcs, which would have confined every diachronic claim to one lineage. Of the four, only Joyce is genuinely blocked (Finnegans Wake not US PD until 2035); James was available throughout. Ford's early work (1906-13) and Faulkner's pre-1931 novels remain unaddressed. Third pass 2026-09-29: added three Standard Ebooks titles — Faulkner's Soldiers' Pay (1926) and Ford's A Man Could Stand Up— (1926) and The Last Post (1928), completing Parade's End. These are hand-proofread e-texts, not OCR; verify_corpus.py gained a Standard Ebooks provenance layer (canonical content.opf from each title's public GitHub repo) since SE's OPDS feeds are gated. Faulkner's Mosquitoes (1927) and Sartoris (1929) remain available only as Internet Archive scans and are deliberately NOT ingested yet — see the OCR control. 2026-10-01: added eight coauthor-supplied texts — Faulkner's Mosquitoes (1927), Sanctuary (1931), Light in August (1932), Pylon (1935) and Absalom, Absalom! (1936), and Pilgrimage volumes 10-12 (Dawn's Left Hand 1931, Clear Horizon 1935, Dimple Hill 1938). No external catalogue holds these, so each carries a provenance_note. A new quote_convention field records that Richardson's volumes 10-12 use single quotes for dialogue where volumes 1-9 use double — a typesetting difference sitting directly on Cohn's L1/L2 boundary, which must be tested for rather than assumed harmless.
